question: Compare how Schwab and Raymond James describe their value proposition to independent advisors.

claims.text: Core positioning - Schwab: On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CFO Michael Verdeschi said Schwab provides "an industry-leading value proposition to individual investors and RIAs," which he tied to approximately 47 million total accounts and approximately $12 trillion in client assets. CEO Rick Wurster said independent advisers "have a great model" because the fiduciary model works, and that "as we're successful in supporting their growth, we win as well."

Core positioning - Raymond James: On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry described a "best of both worlds value proposition." He said it combines an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions, and that the strong balance sheet and commitment to independence are increasingly a differentiator. On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), he cited the largest addressable market across affiliation options (employee, independent contractor, RIA custody), plus cultural fit and the platform. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), he said balance sheet, long-term focus and commitment to independence set the firm apart, and he pointed to near-record adviser satisfaction.

Core positioning - Raymond James: The firm's independent advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-05-19) frames the offer as "A partnership in independence." It says an independent contractor affiliate can "access our full capabilities at a level that's right for your business" and that "Everything we have is yours when you want it."

Services and capabilities for independent advisors - Schwab: The 2Q26 10-Q (published August 2026) says the Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors and recordkeepers. Schwab says its strategy is "Through Clients' Eyes." Separately, the Schwab Advisor Network disclosure (investor day deck, May 2026) says Schwab prescreens independent advisors for referrals, advisors pay fees to Schwab in connection with referrals, and Schwab does not supervise them.

Services and capabilities for independent advisors - Raymond James: The independent advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-05-19) describes a "full-service, self-clearing New York Stock Exchange-member broker/dealer." It lists investing, planning, private wealth, marketing and technology, including private wealth concierge support and "advisor tech shaped by advisors." On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Shoukry said the firm is investing in private wealth tools and in automation, process improvement and AI, as part of a more than $1.1 billion annual technology spend.

Differentiators and competitive set - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published February 2026) says that in Advisor Services Schwab competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks and trust companies. Across both segments it names scale and size as a key competitive advantage, and it cites $11.90 trillion in client assets.

Differentiators and competitive set - Raymond James: The firm's affiliation-options page (page content as of 2026-04-21) presents AdvisorChoice®, a range of options that includes Independent Contractor and Corporate RIA. The firm says each is backed by "a leading independent financial firm." The 2025 investor day deck (June 2025) shows the independent contractor and RIA & custody services options within the AdvisorChoice spectrum. The FY2025 10-K (published November 2025) says its ability to attract advisors rests on its values-based culture, commitment to service, and the unique ways it provides services to advisors, and it describes separate national conferences for the independent contractor and employee channels.

adjacent.text: WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) reported that Schwab CEO Rick Wurster, speaking at Schwab Impact, said Schwab wants RIAs to have equal or better access than wirehouse counterparts to lending, private-market investing and long-short strategies. He is quoted as saying Schwab is "increasingly trying to play a role of being their bank."
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) reported that Shoukry said Raymond James has the largest total addressable market because it offers all affiliation options at scale. He said advisors do not have to select a channel and can focus on cultural fit and capabilities. It also reported that the independent contractor channel is drawing the most interest by dollar volume.
